confusions: The tax and spending pages ran to many screens, so finding the top 1% share over 1999-00 to 2023-24 took most of my 40 actions and I still never reached the wealth tax figures.
The 'Debt' menu link took me to a page on borrowing costs rather than the debt history, so I had to go in through Questions.
Tapping a link in the text or 'On this page' sometimes sent me to a glossary entry or a sources list instead of the answer I wanted.
Pressing back took me to the question list rather than to the page I had just left, so I lost my place.
I could not find where the site talks about the OECD's reform package, so that question stayed unanswered.
The manifesto page is 26 screens long and the pledges are only reachable by scrolling or tapping through a list, which wore me out.
The sources list is grouped by publisher and I could not tell which entry matched the figure I was checking.
The welfare and pensions figures were not where I expected, and I ran out of actions before I found them.
The Labour pledge ratings ('kept', 'partly kept', 'not kept') were clear enough, but I had to open each pledge to see why, which took time.
The housing page gave ownership by tenure for each year, so I had to add two chart values by hand to compare 2008-09 with 2024-25.
The site did not say outright how many years of pay a deposit would take, so I was left doing sums in my head and I don't trust sums I have to do myself.
I am not sure of the number of taxpayers that matches one per cent of receipts, because that part of the high earners page was not one I got to read.
